--- PART 1/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective." / "Parent is fairly cooperative, punishes recent D. We can improve by better exploitation of pure cooperators and endgame, while maintaining cooperation with reciprocators."
STRATEGY: Parent is cooperative, punishes recent defections, and forgives. The trace simulates iterated PD against mixed opponents (always C, always D, TFT, grudger, random) and designs a new strategy with early probing, exploitation of non-retaliating cooperators, punishment of defectors, and last-round defection.

--- PART 2/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice says avoid permanent retaliation, forgive isolated defection. So in our logic, when last_opp=='D' and last_me=='C', we should probably cooperate, not defect, unless opponent has been defecting frequently."
STRATEGY: The parent is a cooperative/forgiving strategy that begins with C, probes/exploits non-punishing opponents, retaliates against defection, and forgives isolated defections. The trace simulates this parent against TFT, always-C, always-D, slot0, slot5, and random opponents, and revises it by adding last-round defection, more forgiveness after being exploited, mutual-defection break-out logic, and occasional exploitation when punishment rate is low.

--- PART 3/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective."
STRATEGY: The parent is a history-based strategy that opens C, probes D at n=1, exploits never-defecting opponents, forgives a single defection, breaks out of mutual defection after a DD streak, and defects on the last round. The trace simulates it against TFT, always D, always C, grudger, and slot11-like opponents, and revises early-round handling, mutual-defection break-out, forgiveness after cooperating into a defection, and endgame behavior.
